notes: §1985:VI.6.27.3 SR7: "Identifier-1 must not be reference modified." VersionConformancePass.VisitUnstringStatement asks IsReferenceModified of every strUnstrSender alternative (the data-name through ReferenceResolver.ReadWritten, and since kb/Work PB5194 the function-identifier's and inline invocation's result refModPart) and gates the construct unstring-sender-reference-modified-2002, refusing it below 2002 with COBOL0900; the function-identifier gap the prior PARTIAL named is closed. Probed at --std 85 (classes a, b, c, d): SRC (1:5), SRC (1:), SRG OF G (1:4), SRT (I) (I:5) and FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (SRC) (1:5) are each refused with COBOL0900; a plain, a subscripted and a function sender, a function whose ARGUMENT is reference-modified, a reference-modified receiver and a reference-modified delimiter compile and split correctly; at --std 2002 SRC (I:5) is accepted. The witness refuses UNSTRING SRC (1:5) with COBOL0900. History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read PARTIAL, naming no kb/Work note; the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5194 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-07.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-07-refute.json).

next.reason: 1985: "Identifier-1 must not be reference modified."; 2023: "No rule in 14.9.48.3 (SR-1 to SR-10) forbids reference modification of identifier-1; only a variable-length group is barred". The 2023 UNSTRING syntax rules, which appear complete, restrict identifier-1 only by category and variable-length group. The ban on reference modification is dropped.
